about: Draft choice note per answer text (lower case, single spaces), used by the bank builder for choice_notes and tip_short. Pipeline only (not exported).

glossary.90 degrees f: A temperature rating near body heat.
glossary.a metal faceplate not less than 0.030 in: A metal cover plate at least 0.030 in. thick.
glossary.a reset type test button on the face of: A test button on the outlet face.
glossary.a single run of cable shall not contain: One cable run limited to four 90-degree bends.
glossary.a supplemental list that shows all invol: A list of every energy source and lockout.
glossary.acceptable: Satisfactory for the inspector and the rule.
glossary.accessible: Can be reached for service (may need tools or a ladder).
glossary.afci: Trips on dangerous arcing that starts fires.
glossary.an adequate path for grounding purposes: A low-resistance fault-current path to ground.
glossary.an orange triangle located on the face o: An orange triangular mark on the outlet face.
glossary.approved: Acceptable to the local inspector (the authority having jurisdiction).
glossary.arc-fault interrupter: Device tripping on dangerous sparking inside walls.
glossary.areas not adaptable as future occupiable: Spaces that can't become living space.
glossary.as a feeder: Use as the subpanel supply conductors.
glossary.as service entrance: Use bringing utility power into the building.
glossary.bonding jumper: A short conductor joining metal parts for fault current.
glossary.branch circuits: Final circuits to outlets and equipment.
glossary.by-pass: A path routed around a device.
glossary.circuit bypass: An unintended alternate path around part of a circuit.
glossary.co/alr: Devices rated for aluminum and copper-clad aluminum wire.
glossary.co/alr orange marking on the face of the: An orange terminal marking for aluminum-rated devices.
glossary.controller: The device that starts and stops a motor.
glossary.damp or wet location: Areas with moisture where NM cable is barred.
glossary.disconnect: A switch that disconnects equipment from power.
glossary.disconnecting means: The switch or breaker opened before servicing equipment.
glossary.disconnection: The act of disconnecting (see disconnecting means).
glossary.dissipation: Heat spreading away from a part.
glossary.dpdt: Double-pole double-throw: two wires flipped between paths.
glossary.dpst: Double-pole single-throw: two wires switched together.
glossary.equipment grounding: The green-wire safety path on receptacles and equipment.
glossary.feeder: Conductors from the service to a subpanel.
glossary.fire-resistant: Withstands fire exposure without quick failure.
glossary.flame-retardant: Self-extinguishing material that stops burning on its own.
glossary.gfci: Trips on tiny current leaks to ground.
glossary.grandfather: Older person or thing; not an NEC-defined term for people.
glossary.gray: Gray insulation marks a grounded (neutral) wire.
glossary.green: Green insulation marks the grounding wire.
glossary.ground fault: Current leaking to ground through an unintended path.
glossary.grounded: Connected to earth (often the white neutral conductor).
glossary.grounded conductor: The white neutral, carrying normal current, connected to earth.
glossary.grounding conductor: Green or bare wire carrying fault current to the source.
glossary.guarded: Shielded or enclosed against accidental contact with live parts.
glossary.harmonic: A multiple-frequency distortion of the AC wave.
glossary.identified: Recognizable as suitable for the purpose by marking, listing, or labeling.
glossary.isolated: Separated from everything else (own path or enclosure).
glossary.it may be mounted flush on a wall in a w: Surface mounting allowed in wet spots.
glossary.it may be used in hazardous locations, w: Allowed in explosive areas when the rules permit.
glossary.it must be at least 1/3 the ampere ratin: At least one-third the big bus rating.
glossary.knowledge that each person involved in t: Every worker controlling their own energy.
glossary.labeled: Carries the mark of a testing lab for a specific purpose.
glossary.lcdi: Leakage-current protection built into appliance cords.
glossary.listed: Tested by a lab (like UL) for a specific use.
glossary.main bonding jumper: The connection joining neutral to ground at the service.
glossary.marked: Carries required text, symbols, or colors on the equipment.
glossary.multifamily dwelling unit: An apartment in a multi-unit building.
glossary.national electrical contractors associat: A trade group of electrical contractors.
glossary.neutral: The grounded conductor (usually white) completing the circuit.
glossary.on a dedicated circuit: The only load on its breaker.
glossary.open circuit: A broken path where no current can flow.
glossary.operator: One who starts, stops, and controls a ride or concession.
glossary.overload: Current above rating lasting long enough to overheat equipment.
glossary.overload protection: Heaters or relays tripping on sustained overload.
glossary.parallel: Wired side-by-side across the same voltage.
glossary.parts changer: Someone swapping parts; not an NEC-defined term.
glossary.people: Human beings on the job site.
glossary.permitted: Allowed by the Code under stated conditions.
glossary.pink: Pink is an allowed color for ungrounded conductors.
glossary.qualified: Trained, skilled, and hazard-aware (a defined person).
glossary.readily accessible: Quick to reach without obstacles or keys.
glossary.recognized: Acknowledged by the Code for an application.
glossary.scale: The ratio of drawing to real size.
glossary.secondary: The stepped-down side of a transformer.
glossary.selective coordination: Staging protective devices so a fault opens only the nearest one.
glossary.series: Wired end-to-end in a single path.
glossary.series-parallel: Groups in series, groups joined in parallel.
glossary.serviceable: Made so it can be maintained or repaired in place.
glossary.short circuit: Hot touching neutral or ground, producing very large current.
glossary.short-circuit: A violent hot-to-neutral or hot-to-ground fault.
glossary.shunt trip: A breaker add-on tripping it from a remote signal.
glossary.sign enclosure: The electrical enclosure part of a sign.
glossary.spdt: Single-pole double-throw: one wire flipped between two paths.
glossary.spst: Single-pole single-throw: one wire in, one out, on/off.
glossary.stamped: Marking pressed or printed into the equipment surface.
glossary.stoow: Extra-hard portable cord, oil- and weather-resistant.
glossary.suitable: Fit for the particular purpose and conditions.
glossary.supplementary: Extra protection beyond the branch rating.
glossary.tap: A short conductor tapped off a feeder.
glossary.termination: The point where a wire lands.
glossary.thhn: Thermoplastic, heat-resistant wire with a nylon jacket.
glossary.transfer: Energy moved from one place to another.
glossary.transition assembly: The listed box joining flat FCC cable to ordinary wiring.
glossary.ungrounded: Not connected to earth (often a hot conductor).
glossary.water resistant: Resists water entry to a rated degree.
glossary.weather proof: Enclosure keeping water out in wet locations.
glossary.weather resistant: Built to survive rain and sun in wet locations.
glossary.where practicable, be located below the: Run under power lines where possible.
glossary.where subject to physical damage: Places where cable can be struck or crushed.
glossary.white: White insulation marks the grounded (neutral) wire.
